findings.claim: Signed commit e02d7b0aa015cda7b1ae24e7eb45066fc3077811 contains the four registrar artifacts and has a verified good ED25519 signature. Every execution-bundle binding resolves to its recorded SHA-256. The execution bundle, registrar event log, registrar boundary receipt and semantic verification stop receipt each produce zero validation errors against their frozen JSON Schemas.
findings.uncertainty: Schema validity establishes contract shape and constants; it does not independently attest to provider-side events outside the committed record.
findings.remediation: Preserve the signed registrar artifacts unchanged.

findings.claim: Independent recomputation finds 208 ordered unique query IDs and texts, 1034 raw result records, 609 unique canonical URLs, exactly matching 609-entry candidate and exposure projections, 329 HTML, 235 file and 45 other exposures, and 329 official-HTML allowlist entries. Every exposure is requested false.
findings.uncertainty: These counts are derived from committed artifacts; the adviser did not observe provider calls.
findings.remediation: Treat them as artifact-backed execution claims, not external network attestation.

findings.claim: The stopped bundle overlaps predecessor exposure. Canonical recomputation finds 10 overlaps in the immediate 31-URL structural-preflight ledger and 23 overlaps across its complete bound 86-URL predecessor chain. All 23 were enumerated in the first issue of this report and remain unavailable for unseen-edition evidence.
findings.uncertainty: Earlier aggregate exposure is incompletely reconstructable, so 23 is a verified lower bound, not complete historical non-overlap.
findings.remediation: Keep the execution terminal and failed; carry all 609 successor exposures and the complete predecessor lineage into any future denylist.

findings.claim: The successor verifier reads only the immediate ledger and does not traverse its bound predecessor. The stop is correct because the immediate set overlaps, but cumulative overlap is undercounted.
findings.uncertainty: The defect does not invalidate the fail-closed outcome; it makes its reason incomplete.
findings.remediation: Prospectively add digest-bound recursive traversal with cycle/depth controls and inherited-overlap tests; do not rewrite the stopped bundle.

findings.claim: The schema-valid bundle, boundary receipt and 209-event log consistently record zero result, landing-page, source-file, HEAD and redirect requests; zero persisted snippets, excerpts and target facts; and no candidate or source-content opening. Result objects contain titles and URLs but no snippet field.
findings.uncertainty: This is consistent digest-bound self-reporting, not an independently captured packet trace or provider audit log.
findings.remediation: Retain the bounded claim and make no broader assertion about provider internals.

findings.claim: Fail-closed stopping was required by the frozen non-overlap contract. The execution cannot proceed to selection or acquisition and supplies no G2 passage evidence.
findings.uncertainty: A future owner decision may authorize a separately frozen lineage but cannot convert this execution into a pass.
findings.remediation: Accept the stop as immutable failed evidence only.

options.description: Accept this execution as terminal failed evidence, fix cumulative-ledger traversal and tests, and separately redesign the candidate frame before any new network activity.
trade_offs: Strongest evidence integrity and simplest lineage.
Requires new owner authorization and does not advance G2 immediately.
limitations: A compliant unseen frame may be infeasible.
options.contingency: If a sufficiently large unexposed frame cannot be frozen without adaptive searching, terminate this holdout route and redesign the evidence question.

options.description: Retain the 609 records only as an exposed metadata census, never as unseen candidates, under a separate future use contract.
trade_offs: Cannot support the blind-holdout claim and adds governance complexity.
limitations: No result becomes rights-cleared or eligible.
options.contingency: If exposed-discovery and unseen-evaluation separation cannot be mechanically enforced, use Option A.

options.description: Preserve the stop and take no further repository action.
trade_offs: G2 remains blocked and the verifier defect remains open.
limitations: Does not improve the frame or verifier.
options.contingency: Return to Option A before any successor design.

recommendation: Choose Option A. Preserve the execution and registrar artifacts unchanged as terminal failed evidence; prospectively correct cumulative exposure traversal and negative tests; construct any future frame only after removing every known exposed URL, edition and series; and return a new digest-bound design to the sole owner before network or source access.
rationale: Immediate-ledger overlap is sufficient to require the stop; 23 cumulative overlaps and incomplete earlier exposure make retrospective acceptance unsafe. Prospective correction preserves auditability.
conflicts: The bundle records no known overlaps, but recomputation finds 10 immediate and 23 cumulative overlaps.
The verifier checks only the immediate ledger although it binds a predecessor chain.
abstentions: No opinion is offered on result relevance, exact-edition identity, rights or structural eligibility.
No network call, result URL, landing page, file or source content was accessed.
